tools.name: find_vessels_in_area
tools.description: Vessels currently inside a latitude/longitude bounding box, newest report first, with optional kind and ship-type filters. Anonymous calls may cover 100 square degrees per call.

kind.description: only this kind: vessel, aton (aid to navigation), base (base station), sar (search and rescue aircraft or distress beacon), or gear (fishing gear); vessel leaves out distress beacons and gear

flag.description: only vessels flying this flag: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. NO, FI, MH

types.description: only these ITU ship type codes, e.g. 30 fishing, 36 sailing, 37 pleasure craft, 52 tug, 60 passenger, 70 cargo, 80 tanker; a code ending in 0 matches its decade, so 70 matches 70 to 79

tools.name: find_vessels_near
tools.description: Vessels within a radius (default 10 NM, maximum 50) of a point or of another vessel's last known position, nearest first, each with distance and bearing from the centre.

lat.description: centre latitude in degrees, paired with lon when the centre is a point

mmsi.description: MMSI of the vessel whose last position is the search centre, instead of lat and lon. Results exclude this vessel

radius_nm.description: search radius in nautical miles: default 10, maximum 50

kind.description: only this kind: vessel, aton, base, sar, or gear; vessel leaves out distress beacons and gear

flag.description: only vessels flying this flag: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. NO, FI, MH

types.description: only these ITU ship type codes; a code ending in 0 matches its decade

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Where Open Waters AIS is hearing AIS right now: sources with their current delay, stations, freshness, and vessel counts. A bounding box adds the stations whose coverage overlaps that area and a count of vessels in it. A station ID adds statistics for that station. Vessel counts cover the last 30 minutes; max_age widens them, to 7d for the last week or all for every vessel the network has heard. An area without reports may have gaps in coverage.

bbox.description: area for station coverage and vessel counts

max_age.description: count vessels heard within this long, network-wide and in bbox, instead of the last 30 minutes: a duration such as 6h, 24h, or 7d, or all for every vessel the network has heard

tools.name: get_vessel_track
tools.description: The positions heard from one vessel over a time range, oldest first, with speed, course, and navigational status. Positions implying an impossible speed for the vessel are left out. A vessel can be identified by MMSI, or by IMO with a feeder or partner token. A call covers up to a year. By default the track is simplified by shape: the positions that hold its path, with breaks where the vessel went unheard; interval_minutes asks for even spacing instead.

mmsi.description: the vessel's MMSI, as an alternative to its IMO number

imo.description: the vessel's IMO number, instead of mmsi; needs a feeder or partner token. Follows the one vessel the IMO names: its only MMSI, or the only one heard in the last 30 days

from.description: start, RFC 3339 UTC; default 24 hours before to. A call covers up to 366 days

interval_minutes.description: at most one position per this many minutes, evenly spaced; by default the track is simplified by shape instead, keeping the positions that hold its path. Anonymous and personal calls reaching past 48 hours are rounded up to whole minutes

limit.description: positions to return: default 50, maximum 200; when more match, the newest are kept

tools.name: get_vessels
tools.description: Last known position and particulars of specific vessels by MMSI (Maritime Mobile Service Identity), or by IMO number with a feeder or partner token: the last report heard for each, however long ago, with destination, ETA, draught, and dimensions once its static data has been heard, and which identifiers match no vessel the network has heard. A vessel whose IMO number has a Wikidata item also carries its type, builder, year built, tonnage, registered dimensions, registry, home port, owner, operator, former names, and Wikipedia and Commons links from there, and a documented US vessel its service type, status, official number, registered dimensions, and tonnage from the US Coast Guard.

mmsi.description: MMSIs to look up; anonymous calls may pass 10 identifiers per call, a personal token 50

imo.description: IMO numbers to look up, counted with mmsi against the same cap; needs a feeder or partner token. Each returns up to 10 vessels that reported it, most recently heard first, and a vessel is found by IMO only once its static data has been heard

tools.name: search_vessels_by_name
tools.description: Vessels whose name contains the text, case-insensitive, among every vessel the network has heard, each with its MMSI and last known position when available. An optional bounding box narrows the search. With a feeder or partner token, text of the form IMO 9241061 finds the vessels reporting that IMO number, and a bare seven-digit number finds them ahead of the name matches.

name.description: text to find in the vessel name, at least 2 characters, case-insensitive; with a feeder or partner token, IMO followed by an IMO number finds that IMO

bbox.description: only vessels whose last position is inside this box

flag.description: only vessels flying this flag: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. NO, FI, MH
